units.name: SSR

power.logic_voltage_status: do not derive GPIO logic voltage from the 5V supply label

protocol.summary: GPIO high energizes the solid-state relay and GPIO low releases it; DIN is the yellow wire, white is NC. There is no address or register map, and the guest can only drive the pad, never read relay state. The official driver uses active-high on()/off()/set_state().
gaps: Zero-cross switching, overcurrent protection, AC-only load behavior and electrical isolation are not modeled.
The product page states the SSR is suitable for AC loads; that must not become a virtual rejection of DC test loads.

units.name: Hall

power.logic_voltage_status: do not derive GPIO logic voltage from the 5V supply label

protocol.summary: Three A3144E Hall switches feed a 74HC08D logic gate; the product specification is low-level active, so a magnet near the sensing face pulls the white wire low and lights the indicator. The driver subclasses PIRUnit: it reads the raw white line, uses IRQ_ACTIVE=0 / IRQ_NEGATIVE=1 and registers both-edge interrupts.
gaps: The three-sensor plus 74HC08D spatial/logic combination is modeled only as one synthetic line level.
Indicator LED, magnetic field strength and pole orientation are not modeled.

units.name: DLight

power.logic_voltage_status: do not derive GPIO logic voltage from the 5V supply label

protocol.summary: I2C 0x23. Single-byte command protocol: power down/on/reset (0x00/0x01/0x07); continuous H-res/H-res2/L-res (0x10/0x11/0x13); one-time H-res/H-res2/L-res (0x20/0x21/0x23); sensitivity is two bytes 0x40|(mt>>5) and 0x60|(mt&0x1F) with mt=int(69*sensitivity). A read returns 2 bytes big-endian raw and the driver converts lux=raw/1.2/sensitivity, dividing by 2 in H-res2.

registers.meaning: sensitivity low byte: (0b011<<5)|(mt&0b11111); then re-issue the measurement command
illuminance raw value; lux=raw/1.2/sensitivity (H-res2 divides by 2 again)

gaps: BH1750FVI datasheet is linked but not reviewed; the power-on default MTreg is unresolved.
The driver _ready() timing expression is questionable and must not be replicated as hardware timing.

The product page claims 1..65535 lx, but the driver's lux=raw/1.2 conversion needs raw=lux*1.2; a 16-bit raw at sensitivity 1 caps near 54612 lx, so the declared top of range is not encodable without MTreg/sensitivity changes. Treat the top boundary as unresolved and clamp fixtures to the encodable range.

units.name: Accel

power.logic_voltage_status: do not derive GPIO logic voltage from the 5V supply label

protocol.summary: I2C 0x53. Register-pointer protocol with auto-increment on multi-byte reads. Driver init writes POWER_CTL(0x2D)=0x08 and INT_ENABLE(0x2E)=0. Acceleration is read as six bytes from 0x32 (X/Y/Z little-endian int16) and converted with raw*0.004*9.80665 m/s2. Interrupt source at 0x30 is read-to-clear.

The DATA_FORMAT range bit effect on raw LSB is unresolved.

units.name: 4Relay

power.logic_voltage_status: do not derive GPIO logic voltage from the 5V supply label

protocol.summary: I2C 0x26, STM32 register device with two registers. 0x10 bit0 selects LED sync mode (0=manual, 1=auto: LEDs follow relay state); 0x10 bits 7..1 are documented read-only. 0x11 holds LED1..4 and RELAY1..4, 1=on 0=off. The official product-page table lists RELAY1 at bit3 / RELAY4 at bit0 and LED1 at bit7 / LED4 at bit4, while both official executable drivers (MicroPython unit/relay4.py and Arduino Unit_4RELAY.cpp) use RELAYn=bit(n-1) and LEDn=bit(n+3). This draft adopts the driver-compatible bit order and records the page-table conflict.

registers.meaning: bit0 LED sync mode: 0 manual, 1 auto; bits 7..1 documented read-only
driver-compatible: bits 3..0 RELAY1..RELAY4, bits 7..4 LED1..LED4, 1=on 0=off; the product-page table lists the reverse bit order (bit3=RELAY1, bit0=RELAY4, bit7=LED1, bit4=LED4)

gaps: Bit-order conflict: the product-page Protocol table (RELAY1=bit3, LED1=bit7) is the reverse of both official executable drivers (RELAY1=bit0, LED1=bit4). This draft uses the driver-compatible order; do not mix the two.
The Python driver set_relay_all(1) writes 0xFF (also lights all LEDs) while the Arduino relayAll() writes 0x0f; that is a driver difference, not a hardware conclusion.
Relay contact timing, load capability and electrical isolation are not modeled.
Behavior when writing the read-only/reserved 0x10 bits is not documented.

PinMap wire colors (yellow=SDA, white=SCL)
inline Protocol table for registers 0x10 and 0x11
register constants, bit positions of relay/LED states and read-modify-write path
